# Verdict: REJECT ## Overall Assessment This component is **completely inaccessible to keyboard-only and screen reader users**. The trigger is a non-focusable `
` with no keyboard event handlers, no ARIA state attributes, and no semantic button role. A mouse-only user can interact with it; everyone else cannot. This is not a partial implementation — the accessibility layer is entirely absent. The two "features present" (visual indicator, onClick) are the minimum for a sighted mouse user and provide zero assistive technology support. ## Pre-commitment Predictions Before reading the code, for a disclosure/expandable section component I predicted: 1. **Trigger is a `
` instead of ` ``` - **Confidence:** HIGH - **Realist Check:** No workaround exists. A keyboard user cannot reach this element. Detection would be immediate in any keyboard test. Severity is correctly CRITICAL — this is not a degraded experience, it is a wall. --- ### 2. No `aria-expanded` — state not communicated to assistive technology **Evidence:** The component tracks `isExpanded` in React state but never exposes it to the DOM: ```jsx const [isExpanded, setIsExpanded] = useState(false); // ... {isExpanded ? ' −' : ' +'} // visual only, no ARIA ``` - **File:** `BuggyExpandable.jsx`, the `isExpanded` state variable and the conditional symbol rendering - **User group impacted:** Screen reader users (NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver) - **WCAG citation:** **4.1.2 Name, Role, Value** — "For all user interface components (including but not limited to: form elements, links and components generated by scripts), name, role, and values can be programmatically determined." - **WAI-ARIA APG citation:** Disclosure (Show/Hide) pattern — "The element that controls the disclosure has `aria-expanded` set to `true` or `false`." - **Why this matters:** A screen reader user who could somehow activate this element (e.g., via a screen reader's "click" command) would hear the title text and "plus" or "minus" — but would have no programmatic indication of whether the section is expanded or collapsed. The `+`/`−` symbols are visual glyphs, not semantic state. VoiceOver would announce "plus" or "minus" as characters, not as state. - **Fix:** Add `aria-expanded={isExpanded}` to the trigger element. This is the single most important ARIA attribute for a disclosure widget. - **Confidence:** HIGH - **Realist Check:** Without this, a screen reader user cannot determine the current state. They would have to guess or rely on whether content follows. Complete state loss. CRITICAL is correct. --- ### 3. No `aria-controls` — trigger not linked to content panel **Evidence:** The content panel: ```jsx {isExpanded && (
{content}
)} ``` - **File:** `BuggyExpandable.jsx`, the conditional content `
` - **User group impacted:** Screen reader users - **WCAG citation:** **1.3.1 Info and Relationships** — "Information, structure, and relationships conveyed through presentation can be programmatically determined." - **WAI-ARIA APG citation:** Disclosure (Show/Hide) pattern — "The element that controls the disclosure has `aria-controls` referencing the `id` of the disclosure content." - **Why this matters:** Without `aria-controls`, a screen reader user cannot navigate from the trigger to the content (or vice versa). The relationship between "this button" and "this panel" is invisible to assistive technology. - **Fix:** Add `aria-controls="expandable-content"` to the trigger and `id="expandable-content"` to the panel. Note: since the panel is conditionally rendered (unmounted when collapsed), the `id` will not exist in the DOM when collapsed. This is acceptable per APG — `aria-controls` may reference an element that is not currently in the DOM. - **Confidence:** HIGH - **Realist Check:** This is a relationship gap, not a complete access loss (the user can still navigate to content via sequential browsing). However, it breaks the expected disclosure interaction model. CRITICAL is defensible; MAJOR is also defensible. I'll keep CRITICAL because combined with finding #1, the entire interaction model is broken for AT users. --- ## Major Findings (Significantly Degrades Experience) ### 4. `+`/`−` symbols announced as characters by screen readers **Evidence:** ```jsx {isExpanded ? ' −' : ' +'} ``` - **File:** `BuggyExpandable.jsx`, the conditional symbol rendering inside the trigger - **User group impacted:** Screen reader users - **WCAG citation:** **1.1.1 Non-text Content** — "All non-text content that is presented to the user has a text alternative that serves the equivalent purpose." - **Why this matters:** Screen readers announce `+` as "plus" and `−` (U+2212) as "minus" or "minus sign." A user hears: *"Section Title, plus"* or *"Section Title, minus."* This is redundant with `aria-expanded` (once added) and confusing without it. The symbols are decorative state indicators, not content. - **Fix:** Wrap in ``: ```jsx {isExpanded ? ' −' : ' +'} ``` - **Confidence:** HIGH - **Realist Check:** This is a minor annoyance layered on top of the critical issues. If `aria-expanded` is added, the symbols become redundant noise. MAJOR is slightly inflated; MINOR is more accurate in isolation, but in the context of a component with zero ARIA, it contributes to the overall confusion. I'll keep MAJOR because it actively misleads AT users about what the symbol means. --- ### 5. No heading structure — section title is not a heading **Evidence:** ```jsx
{title} ``` - **File:** `BuggyExpandable.jsx`, the title rendering - **User group impacted:** Screen reader users (heading navigation), cognitive users (information architecture) - **WCAG citation:** **1.3.1 Info and Relationships** — structure and relationships must be programmatically determinable. - **WAI-ARIA APG citation:** Disclosure (Show/Hide) pattern — "The heading element contains the button that controls the disclosure." - **Why this matters:** Screen reader users navigate by headings (H key in NVDA, VO+Up/Down in VoiceOver). Content panel has no `role="region"` or accessible name **Evidence:** ```jsx

The trigger button should have an `id` (e.g., `id="expandable-trigger"`) so the panel can reference it via `aria-labelledby="expandable-trigger"`. ### 8.
